subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should changing output from a completed nonzero exec count as progress, or should every same-command result with the same nonzero exit metadata be treated as identical?
rationale: Both choices affect availability: output-sensitive hashing permits volatile retry loops, while unconditional output removal can terminate legitimate recovery workflows, so automation should not select the product policy.

options.title: Preserve normalized progress
options.body: Keep a bounded normalized output signal for completed nonzero exits while stripping known timestamps and per-attempt identifiers so genuine progress resets the streak.

options.title: Accept output-insensitive failures
options.body: Treat all completed nonzero results with the same structured metadata as no progress and explicitly accept the legitimate-retry false-positive risk.

recommendation.title: Preserve normalized progress
recommendation.body: Keep a bounded normalized output signal for completed nonzero exits while stripping known timestamps and per-attempt identifiers so genuine progress resets the streak.
